question: Students of Engineering college of ______ developed a Satellite named as "SriShaktiSat" for ISRO in Jan, 2021.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Coimbatore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The students of Sri Shakthi Institute of Engineering and Technology in **Coimbatore** developed the satellite named "SriShaktiSat".
 
• It was developed as part of a collaborative project with the Indian Space Research Organisation (**ISRO**).
 
• The satellite aims to help with communication and other space-related research.
 
• This project marks a significant achievement for the students and the institution, showcasing their technical skills and innovation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**

 
 
• ISRO is the space agency of the Government of India, headquartered in Bengaluru.
 
• It was founded in 1969 and has achieved numerous milestones in space research and development.
 
• ISRO's missions include launching satellites for communication, weather forecasting, and navigation, as well as planetary exploration missions like Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission).
 
• ISRO has also launched various educational satellite programs to involve students in space research and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Communication**
 
 
• Satellite communication involves the use of artificial satellites to relay and amplify radio telecommunications signals via transponders.
 
• It provides communication capabilities across long distances and is used for television, radio broadcasting, internet services, and military applications.
 
• Satellites play a crucial role in global communication networks, enabling services in remote and rural areas where terrestrial infrastructure is limited.
 
 
 
• **Educational Satellite Programs**
 
 
• Educational satellite programs are initiatives by educational institutions and space agencies to involve students in space technology and research.
 
• These programs provide hands-on experience in satellite design, development, and operations.
 
• They aim to inspire and educate the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space enthusiasts.
 
• Examples include CubeSats, small satellites developed by universities, and collaborative projects with space agencies like ISRO and NASA.
